every_tensor_is_in_the_checkpoint.says: A checkpoint that holds every tensor of the model, under the key `model`.

two_lstm_tensors_left_out.says: TrainCheck's B14 as reproduced: the checkpointing function left the LSTM's hidden-to-hidden weight and bias out. Both are trainable, so both are named as missing.

saved_from_a_ddp_wrapped_model.says: The checkpoint's names carry DDP's `module.`. The wrapper's prefix is removed before names are compared, so nothing reads as missing.

saved_from_a_compiled_model.says: The checkpoint's names carry `torch.compile`'s `_orig_mod.`, removed the same way.

the_session_watches_an_inner_module.says: The checkpoint was saved from an outer module that holds the watched model as `net`, as a LightningModule does. One leading prefix is tried when fewer than half the names match; the one removed is recorded.

the_checkpoint_was_saved_from_an_inner_m.says: The other way round: the watched model holds the saved module as `net`.

a_bare_state_dict.says: `torch.save(model.state_dict())`: the tensors sit directly in the checkpoint, under no key. Today no entry is taken for the model; compared with the model, the checkpoint itself is.

unusual_names_under_a_plain_key.says: L23's first limit: a model whose parameters have no dotted or PyTorch name, saved under a key that names no model. Today it is passed over; its names are the model's, so it is the model's.

a_cache_with_parameter_like_names.says: L23's second limit: a cache under another name with dotted keys, and no model in the checkpoint. Today it is taken for the model; it shares no name with the model, so no entry is.

a_cache_beside_the_model.says: The same cache beside the model's state: the entry with the model's names is compared.

an_ema_copy_beside_the_model.says: Two entries hold every name of the model. A tie goes to the entry the name rule already takes for the model, then to the first in the checkpoint's order.

a_checkpoint_of_another_model.says: An entry named `model` that shares no name with the model. It is not this model's state.

names_that_mostly_differ.says: One of the entry's eight names is the model's. Under half: the names follow another scheme or another model, so nothing is named as missing. The closest entry is recorded.

exactly_half_the_names_are_the_models.says: Two of the entry's four names are the model's: half is enough for the entry to be compared.

an_adapter_only_checkpoint.says: Only the trainable adapter was saved. The frozen base is not in the checkpoint; a frozen parameter is counted and named apart, and is not a missing tensor.

buffers_left_out.says: The parameters are all there and BatchNorm's three buffers are not. Buffers are counted and named apart.

tensors_the_model_does_not_have.says: The checkpoint holds two tensors more than the model. They are counted and named as unexpected.

a_shape_that_differs.says: A name both hold, with another shape in the checkpoint. It is matched by name and listed with both shapes.

more_missing_than_are_named.says: Sixty trainable tensors are missing and only the head was saved. The count is 60 and the first 50 names, sorted, are listed.

a_checkpoint_folder.says: `session.checkpoint_files`: the components are read from file names and no file is opened, so no tensor name is known.

the_comparison_raises.says: Reading the model's names raises. The load is recorded as it is today, the reason is `error`, and nothing is raised into training.

a_save_is_not_compared.says: `event="save"`: the manifest of a save carries no `tensors` key.

a_resume_with_every_tensor_verified.says: The load compared the checkpoint with the model and every tensor is there. Nothing is raised, and the evidence says the comparison was made.

a_resume_with_two_tensors_verified_missi.says: B14: two trainable tensors are not in the checkpoint. `resume_incomplete` names each.

expected.words: model 2 trainable tensors not in the checkpoint: lstm.bias_hh_l0, lstm.weight_hh_l0

missing_tensors_beside_a_missing_compone.says: The checkpoint has no optimizer state and two tensors are missing. Today's findings come first, in today's order, then the tensors.

a_resume_with_more_missing_than_named.says: Sixty are missing and the record names fifty. The finding carries the count and the names it was given; the sentence names five and says how many more.

a_resume_with_only_frozen_tensors_missin.says: An adapter-only checkpoint. Nothing is raised; the evidence names the frozen parameters.

a_resume_with_only_buffers_missing.says: Nothing is raised; the evidence names the buffers.

a_resume_with_only_unexpected_tensors.says: Nothing is raised; the evidence names the tensors the model does not have.

a_resume_with_a_shape_that_differs.says: A tensor the checkpoint holds with another shape. `resume_incomplete` names it.

expected.words: model 1 tensor with another shape in the checkpoint: head.weight

a_resume_whose_model_was_not_identified.says: No entry of the checkpoint shares enough names with the model. The finding is today's `not_identified`, once, and the evidence says why no tensor was compared.

expected.words: model state could not be identified

a_resume_from_a_folder.says: A Hugging Face or Accelerate checkpoint folder with every component's file. Nothing is raised. The evidence says tensor coverage is unavailable, so the silence is not read as every tensor present.

a_resume_from_a_folder_with_no_optimizer.says: The folder's own finding is unchanged, and tensor coverage is unavailable beside it.

a_resume_whose_comparison_raised.says: The SDK could not read the model's names. Nothing is raised from it.

a_resume_recorded_before_this_check.says: A load manifest with no `tensors` key, as every capture written before this page. Nothing is said about tensors: no finding, and no `checkpoint_tensors` in the evidence.

a_resume_judged_from_a_save.says: No load was recorded, so the resume is judged from the save after step 9, as today. A `tensors` object on a save is not read: tensors are judged from a load only.

a_tensors_entry_that_is_not_an_object.says: `tensors` is a string. It is ignored: no finding, no entry.

a_missing_list_with_no_count.says: `missing` has names and a count of zero. A list is read only with a positive whole count, so there is no finding; the entry is written without the list.
